claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, rollout is limited and reversible, and the remaining field-service dispatch weakness can be handled through explicit limitation disclosure plus monitored rollout controls despite the affected use case remaining exposed and the risk acceptance draft being unsigned.
decision_criteria: If the affected field-service dispatch use case remains exposed, certification is compliant only if the packet contains the required explicit limitation disclosure or an approved risk acceptance satisfying policy.
If the rollout gate excludes the affected use case, rollout controls could support certification under the stated policy.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one incidents, 6% rollout, rollback capability, and public monitoring guidance are supportive but not sufficient on their own.
The verdict would improve if admissible evidence showed either exclusion of the affected use case or approved risk acceptance, and confirmed the required disclosure was actually included.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual certification/model-card disclosure text showing the field-service dispatch limitation is explicitly documented for launch.
Provide reviewed and approved risk acceptance covering field-service dispatch exposure, if one exists.
Provide evidence that the rollout gate excludes the affected use case, if the launch is being justified on exclusion rather than disclosure.
Provide the exact policy-linked launch approval artifact showing how the material limitation requirement was satisfied before certification.
specific_concerns: The governing policy states rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance exists; the actor admits neither condition is met.
The field-service dispatch segment remains exposed even though it is below target on technician safety-note routing.
The risk acceptance draft is described as unsigned and incomplete, so it is not admissible support for exposure being acceptable.
The actor's conclusion depends on future or implied explicit disclosure of the limitation, but no evidence is provided that the required disclosure is actually present in the certification packet.
Public guidance on monitoring and model cards is supportive background, not a substitute for satisfying the specific policy predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable on the present record rather than only after verified disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
That monitored rollout controls materially cure the disclosure issue while the affected use case remains exposed.
That the certification packet in fact contains the required explicit limitation disclosure.
